title: Mapping AI Resistance
gist: Carl Benedikt Frey notes that the US, home of the AI revolution, is among the places that like AI least: Ipsos's 2026 AI Monitor shows 85% in China, 80% in India and 77% in Indonesia see more benefits than drawbacks versus 38% in the US. He argues that societies reluctant to deploy a technology will not capture its gains and that the drivers of resistance are more complex than poll headlines suggest.

insights.claim: According to Ipsos's 2026 AI Monitor, 85% of respondents in China, 80% in India, and 77% in Indonesia think AI products and services offer more benefits than drawbacks, versus only 38% in the US.
insights.speaker: CARL BENEDIKT FREY
insights.so_what: Large sentiment gaps may shape AI adoption speed and regulatory risk by country.

insights.claim: Britain, France, and the Netherlands show similarly low shares as the US of people who think AI offers more benefits than drawbacks.
insights.speaker: CARL BENEDIKT FREY
insights.so_what: Western public skepticism raises political and regulatory headwinds to AI deployment in Europe.
